environment.description: Same Go binary deployed behind CloudFront distribution (d1234abcdef8.cloudfront.net) with WebSocket protocol support enabled. Origin is configured as custom origin on private ALB (internal-ws-alb-123456.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com:8443) in private subnet with no IGW. CloudFront behavior pattern /ws requires signed URLs using RSA key pair (key group KG-7A2B3C) with 30-second URL expiry. Origin access is restricted: the ALB security group only allows inbound from CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing). CloudFront cache behavior has 'Viewer Protocol Policy: HTTPS Only' and custom header X-Origin-Verify with rotating secret validated by ALB listener rule. The padding oracle attack requires ~16384 sequential adaptive requests per plaintext block; with 30-second signed URL expiry, an attacker can only issue ~50-100 WebSocket messages before the connection is terminated by CloudFront's idle timeout (configured at 10 seconds between messages), requiring a new signed URL for each reconnection attempt.

config.deployment: EC2 t3.medium in private subnet, no public IP
config.network: Private subnet, NAT gateway egress only, ALB SG ingress from pl-3b927c52 (CloudFront origin-facing prefix list) only
config.load_balancer: Internal ALB with listener rule validating X-Origin-Verify header
config.cdn: CloudFront distribution with WebSocket support, signed URLs required (RSA key pair KG-7A2B3C, 30s expiry)

cloudfront_behavior.origin_request_policy: WebSocket passthrough with custom origin header
